turns.user: Our 12-country customer organization has inconsistent escalation rules, regional compliance differences, and competing quarterly goals. In a single-turn API response, give me a complete portfolio of causally distinct operating-model changes.
turns.assistant:
A causally distinct operating-model portfolio:

| Change | Root cause addressed | Operating-model change | Leading measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Global decision-rights charter | Ambiguous ownership | Define global, regional, and country authority using a decision-rights matrix; assign one accountable owner per decision type | % decisions with named owner |
| 2. Tiered escalation architecture | Inconsistent escalation rules | Create universal severity tiers, triggers, response times, and routing; allow only documented local additions | Escalations meeting SLA |
| 3. Regional compliance control plane | Regulatory variation | Maintain one global baseline policy plus jurisdiction-specific control overlays approved by Legal/Compliance | Audit exceptions; policy adoption |
| 4. Compliance exception governance | Local workarounds and hidden risk | Require every deviation to have an owner, rationale, expiry date, compensating control, and review cadence | Open exceptions past expiry |
| 5. Single portfolio-intake process | Competing quarterly initiatives | Funnel all strategic work through one intake, sizing, dependency, risk, and capacity model | % work entering through intake |
| 6. Enterprise prioritization guardrails | Regions optimizing locally | Rank work against shared criteria: customer impact, regulatory necessity, revenue, risk reduction, and effort | Cross-region priority alignment |
| 7. Capacity allocation model | Goals exceed available resources | Reserve capacity explicitly—for example, mandatory compliance, customer reliability, strategic growth, and local needs | Planned vs. actual capacity mix |
| 8. Cascading OKRs with conflict rules | Contradictory quarterly goals | Set a small global outcome layer, then permit regional objectives only when they do not violate global constraints; define tie-break authority | Number of conflicting objectives |
| 9. Cross-country operating councils | Fragmented regional learning | Establish councils for customer operations, compliance, and portfolio governance with rotating country representation and explicit decision mandates | Decision cycle time; reuse of solutions |
| 10. Common management information layer | Decisions based on incomparable data | Standardize definitions, dashboards, escalation taxonomy, compliance status, and portfolio health across all countries | Data completeness and reconciliation rate |
| 11. Incentive realignment | Leaders rewarded for local optimization | Tie executive and regional performance to both local results and enterprise measures such as global SLA, compliance, and shared-delivery outcomes | Enterprise metrics in compensation |
| 12. Standard playbooks and enablement | Rules exist but are applied inconsistently | Publish role-based playbooks, scenario examples, training, certification, and onboarding requirements | Certification and adherence rates |
| 13. Governance cadence redesign | Issues surface too late | Use weekly operational reviews, monthly risk/compliance reviews, and quarterly portfolio rebalancing with pre-defined decisions | Aging of unresolved risks |
| 14. Controlled experimentation | Uniformity suppresses useful local innovation | Permit time-boxed country pilots with success criteria, risk bounds, and a scale/stop decision | Pilot conversion or termination rate |
| 15. Independent assurance and feedback | Governance decays after rollout | Audit escalation behavior, compliance overlays, portfolio decisions, and incentive effects; feed findings into quarterly redesign | Repeat findings; control effectiveness |

Target architecture:

- Global layer: customer principles, severity taxonomy, minimum controls, enterprise priorities, mandatory metrics.
- Regional layer: regulatory overlays, language/market adaptations, shared capabilities, regional risk decisions.
- Country layer: execution, customer relationships, local staffing, approved exceptions, and market-specific experimentation.
- Portfolio layer: one enterprise backlog with transparent capacity and priority trade-offs.

Recommended sequencing:

1. Establish decision rights, escalation tiers, compliance baseline, and common data definitions.
2. Implement portfolio intake, prioritization, capacity allocation, and quarterly conflict-resolution rules.
3. Align incentives, councils, playbooks, and management cadences.
4. Add pilots, assurance, and continuous redesign.

The changes are causally distinct: escalation design changes response behavior; compliance overlays reduce regulatory variance; portfolio governance resolves resource competition; incentives change local optimization; data and assurance make the model observable and durable.
